_comment: Copy this to accounts.json (GITIGNORED) to hold MULTIPLE named accounts per platform for the hub's <prefix>_account_* tools. env values may be literal secrets OR ${ENV} references resolved from the hub's environment at spawn time. Prefer ${ENV} refs so this file stays secret-free. Env-mode platforms: runpod, kaggle, modal, lightning, ovh, rclone, databricks, biomni. CLI-mode platforms (azure, gcloud) need NO entries here -- their accounts are the CLI's own profiles (az subscriptions / gcloud configurations) and are managed live via the az_/gc_ account tools. If an env-mode platform is omitted and ALL its registration (seed_env) vars are present in the hub env, the hub seeds a single in-memory 'default' account automatically -- EXCEPT rclone, which has no seed_env (its RCLONE_URL comes from spec.env, so it never auto-seeds a default). OVH note: each ovh account bundles OVH_ENDPOINT (ovh-eu | ovh-ca | ovh-us) alongside its creds, so ov_account_switch flips BOTH region and credentials. Creds may be the API-key trio (OVH_APPLICATION_KEY/SECRET/CONSUMER_KEY -- create at ovh.com/auth/api/createToken) OR OAuth2 (OVH_CLIENT_ID/OVH_CLIENT_SECRET); the env bundle is auth-agnostic. Databricks note: each databricks account bundles DATABRICKS_HOST + creds per workspace, so db_account_switch flips BOTH the workspace URL and its credentials. Creds may be a PAT (DATABRICKS_TOKEN) OR an OAuth M2M service principal (DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID/DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET); the SDK's unified auth resolves whichever is present. Biomni note: a biomni account carries EITHER a static BIOMNI_TOKEN (a Bearer access token from a signed-in biomni.phylo.bio session -- expires, refresh by hand) OR a BIOMNI_REFRESH_TOKEN (from the OAuth device-code flow: run bm_auth_login, approve in a browser, bm_auth_poll -- the connector then auto-mints access tokens from it via signin.phylo.bio/oauth2/token, so it stops expiring). Give each account a label (the account email) so bm_account_list shows which is which; bm_account_switch|cycle rotates between them (pair with bm_billing_balance to rotate before one runs dry). bm_auth_status reports the active auth source (tokens masked). Modal note: an md account may also carry MODAL_ENVIRONMENT (the Modal workspace environment name), threaded as MODAL_ENVIRONMENT / the CLI --env. Additionally every modal_* tool accepts an OPTIONAL per-call account/environment arg for concurrency-safe rotation WITHOUT switching the active account: account=<name> resolves MODAL_TOKEN_ID_<NAME>/MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET_<NAME> (optional MODAL_ENVIRONMENT_<NAME>) from the hub environment, else a [<name>] profile in ~/.modal.toml, and builds a per-call modal.Client for THAT call only -- so those env vars (e.g. MODAL_TOKEN_ID_TEAM) must be present in the hub's environment for a named per-call profile to resolve.

aws._comment: AWS is the ONLY env-mode platform here that is inherently SECRET-FREE: AWS_PROFILE + AWS_REGION are just NAMES, so literal values are safe. The actual credential is the IAM Identity Center SSO token in ~/.aws/sso/cache (minted by `aws sso login --sso-session <name>`), which the mcp-proxy-for-aws child resolves from the local botocore chain per request -- it never passes through this file. Each account = one ~/.aws/config [profile]; aws_account_switch respawns the proxy with a different AWS_PROFILE, so it flips BOTH the AWS account and the assumed role. One `aws sso login` covers every profile sharing an sso_start_url, and expiry needs a browser re-login (no watchdog can fix that) -- an expired token surfaces as a per-call token error, not a dead backend.
